confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on web searches of aggregated cost-of-living sites for Koh Lanta, including Wise, CityCost, Numbeo, Stamped Nomad and Traveltables. These sources broadly agree: an inexpensive meal costs about $3 to $3.70, a cappuccino about $2 to $2.50 (Numbeo lists about 97 THB), a local beer $1.60 to $3, and a mid-range meal for two $36 to $41. I rounded slightly toward tourist-area prices. Some of this data is crowd-sourced, thin or a few years old. For example, Numbeo was last updated in April 2025 and notes few contributors. The beer price uses a 2026 budget guide that lists Chang beer at 80 to 120 THB in restaurants. Koh Lanta beer is usually served in bottles, so the 'draft' definition is only approximate. The cocktail price uses the same guide, which lists cocktails at 150 to 250 THB. Wine is the weakest food and drink anchor. I found only one user review that mentions house wine at 180 THB a glass. Imported wine in Thailand is heavily taxed, so I estimated about 190 to 210 THB, or roughly 2.3 times the price of a beer. I converted baht at about 35 THB per USD, as cited by the guide. The accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge, not from searches or listings. They reflect July, which is green/low season on Koh Lanta, when some venues close and room rates are noticeably lower than in high season. The RBA rate of 0.6720 for 18 Nov 2026 comes from a search summary that attributes it to the RBA's 4pm indicative rate. A third-party site, ozfinancehub.com.au, shows the same value. I could not confirm it on the RBA page itself.
comparable_city_reasoning: Koh Lanta is a mid-range Andaman Sea resort island in Krabi province. Food and drink prices sit slightly above mainland Krabi and below Phuket and Koh Phi Phi. I benchmarked the accommodation estimates against Ao Nang, Koh Phangan and Koh Lipe, adjusted for July low-season rates.
